_why: This repository's lanes: the domains inside it that work is dispatched to, each owning its paths (D115, docs/2026-10-01-self-development-design.md §2.1; the map of docs/2026-09-30-parallel-development-design.md §5, which a test holds to this file by id and title). Today tools/merge-branch.mjs reads it, prints which lanes a branch touched, and never refuses a merge on it; the driver, its queue and `connect` are to read it as DEV4 to DEV6 land. `id` is how work addresses a lane: lower-case letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter, unique here. `title` and `summary` are for the people and agents that address it. A path belongs to the first lane that owns it, the steward's before the rest. `steward` marks the one lane that keeps the records, which a lane session never edits. `gates` names the declared gates a landing of that lane alone needs; absent is every gate, only the steward's narrows, and the merge tool chooses gates by its own lane table (GATE3), with the full set owed before a stage. `laneless` lists what belongs to no lane on purpose, each group with its reason; a test refuses a tracked file that is in no lane and not listed there, so a new path is placed when it is added, never left outside silently (LEFT1). A repeated or malformed id, a lane with no paths, two stewards, or a gate nobody declared makes the file unreadable. The rooms (docs/2026-10-26-tree-pool-design.md R5.3, R5.4): a lane with `builds` or a `room` is a room, its own or the one its `room` names, so the two web lanes keep their names and are one room; a laneless group naming a `room` is part of it, and one naming none is in no room. `builds` lists its `units` (the project and package files whose folders hold its sources), what its builds `reads` outside them and what they `writes`, in the gates file's path grammar; the room check (the driver's `RoomCheck`) refuses a malformed or overlapping declaration and joins rooms whose builds meet into one claim group. Nothing acts on the rooms yet; the canon knowledge `rooms-and-classes` says how to declare them. Globs: `*` stays inside one folder, `**` crosses folders, `{a,b}` is either, and a path starting `!` carves a narrower lane's files out of a wider one.

lanes.title: Web shell
lanes.summary: The page but its Settings: the frame, the bridge, the atoms, the work frame, every other screen, the modules they share, the catalogues outside Settings' areas, and the page's build and end-to-end suite.

lanes.title: Web settings
lanes.summary: The Settings screen: its frame, one file per domain, and its catalogue areas.

lanes.title: Driver library
lanes.summary: The driver library, its headless host, its git doors' and partner launcher's programs and their tests: the loop and planner, trees and landing, plugins and hooks, help, the toolchain.

lanes.title: Desktop modules
lanes.summary: The modules the page talks to, the application, the launcher that starts it, and the desktop tree's package versions.
lanes._why: The launcher (D93) is a twin of the modules' taskbar identity (D108). The desktop tree's package versions are the kit the application and the modules run on; the driver has one package of its own, the desktop store's SQLite, pinned beside them (FOUNDATION1 z-i).

lanes.title: Service
lanes.summary: The cross-repository knowledge service, whole: its core, its hosts, its tests and the declaration of its HTTP API.

lanes.title: Ports and testing
lanes.summary: The effect contracts the application depends on, the fakes and contract cases that hold each to its real adapter, and the build settings and banned effects that keep the application off real effects. Each adapter package joins as its row lands.

lanes.title: CLI
lanes.summary: The npm package daoris, whole: its sources, its entry point and its tests.

lanes.title: Tools
lanes.summary: This repository's own tooling and gates: tools/, the devkit, the gates' declaration and the release workflow that runs them, and the workspace's scripts and ignore rules.
lanes._why: The desktop suites' Process settings are here because the gates name them (MOD8). The records were this lane's until DEV2 gave them a lane of their own.

lanes.title: Records
lanes.summary: The backlog, its archive, and this map: the steward's records, which a lane session never edits.
lanes._why: The steward's lane (D115 §5), holding what the parent's list held and the map itself. The parent keeps them as the steward until a steward session does (DEV9). A landing of this lane alone needs the universal gates, which scan and link-check its files, and the cli gate, whose verify reads them: the budgets, the duplicate check and the lanes test.

laneless.what: The docs: read by every lane and written by the change that makes them stale. The steward's archive is carved out: it is the records lane's.
The doctrine and what it is synced into: a canon change re-syncs this repository's own copy and the example family in the same commit, whichever lane asked for it.
The harnesses' settings for working in this repository.
Build settings every desktop project shares, the driver's and the modules' alike, and the analyzers' settings they all read.
Build settings every .NET project of the repository builds with, each tree's importing them: the commit stamped only where a publish builds.
